content:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: elevated 502/504 from az-b (us-west-2b) across multiple services. Alert rule: http5xx_rate > 5% for 2m.
ops-bot: Affected ASGs: inference-azb-*, nat-gw-azb-1 shown healthy but high connection reset counts.
sanjay (oncall-azb): I'm on it — looking at LB & nat metrics. first check: are we seeing route flips?
maya (infra): I see a recent RouteTable update pushed ~6m ago to rt-azb-0 (user: terraform-ci). Change: removed propagated route to nat-gw-legacy and added explicit target nat-gw-azb-1.
lia (sre): customers reporting steady 502s from inference endpoints, roughly 12% of requests from az-b. TL;DR: partial egress blackhole + stale conn tracking.
derek (netops): Confirming: VPC flow logs show a lot of established flows hitting nat-gw-azb-1 but responses not making it back for a subset — symmetric path mismatch.
support-engineer: We have ~18 support tickets mentioning timeouts and upload fails, some customers on older SDKs. Notified sales for high-touch customers.
sanjay (oncall-azb): Any recent NAT re-associations or ENI moves?
maya (infra): Yes, terraform state shows nat-gw-azb-1 was created and associated to rt-azb-0 at 2167889900 (≈3m before alerts). nat-gw-legacy was disassociated.
derek (netops): Hypothesis: connection-tracking still bound to legacy NAT instances/ENIs, and route flip sent traffic to different AZ NAT where CT doesn't match -> return path lost.
lia (sre): That matches traceroutes from affected clients — ICMP shows asymmetric hop count. Also dns lookups for backend service are fine (no TTL churn).
sanjay (oncall-azb): Quick mitigation options: 1) Re-associate route back to nat-gw-legacy (rollback) 2) Force a quick NAT recycle (recreate/replace nat-gw-azb-1) 3) BFD-style failover: route to cross-AZ nat (higher latency)
maya (infra): Rolling back route is fastest and least risky. But terraform drift might reapply — will lock infra changes.
derek (netops): If we rollback, we should also drain/terminate any stale NAT instances (conntrack flush) if using nat instances; for managed NAT gateways we can re-associate and that should be atomic.
lia (sre): Is this a managed NAT GW or NAT instance?
maya (infra): It's a mix — az-b used a managed NAT GW dual-stack fronting some legacy nat instances. The legacy NIs still have conntracked sessions.
sanjay (oncall-azb): OK proceed: Maya will re-associate route table to nat-gw-legacy, I will coordinate with Derek to flush conntrack on legacy instances and restart network daemons. Lia will watch error rates and customer impact.
maya (infra): Executing rollback now:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abcd1234 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-gw-legacy
```
...running
maya (infra): route replace accepted — propagation in progress. Locking terraform workspace to prevent churn: `tf lock apply` (manual hold).
derek (netops): Running conntrack flush on nat instances (legacy pool):
```
for i in $(aws ec2 describe-instances --filters ...); do ssh ec2-user@$i sudo conntrack -F; sudo systemctl restart systemd-networkd || true; done
```
...started.
lia (sre): Error rate dropping from 12% -> 3% in 90s. Latency back to baseline on most endpoints. Watching for secondary spikes.
support-engineer: Notifying customers: sending status update to affected customers now. Preparing follow-up for those on older SDKs.
customer-bot: Sent broadcast status: "Investigating partial egress issue in us-west-2b impacting API calls; mitigation in progress."
sanjay (oncall-azb): Good catch. Next: we need RCA items — root cause seems to be a terraform-driven route swap that didn't account for legacy NAT instance conntrack affinity. Immediate action: revert change and lock.
maya (infra): I already locked the workspace. Will open a PR to update the plan: add a precondition check for active conntrack drain and a canary window.
derek (netops): Long-term: prefer single logical nat per AZ (managed) or add layer that drains CT before route swap. Also consider using route priority with healthcheck-based failover.
sanjay (oncall-azb): Handoff: Lia will continue monitoring for 30m. I'll update incident tracker INC-2427 with mitigation and affected customer list. Lia — take oncall after 02:00 UTC if everything stays green else ping me.
lia (sre): Taking monitoring. Will escalate if >1% 5xx persists for 10m.
maya (infra): Postmortem notes: affected by terraform apply that created nat-gw-azb-1 and updated RT without draining legacy NAT instances. Action items: policy to require canary route and conntrack drain, infra automation tests, update runbook.
support-engineer: Logged customers impacted: CUST-112, CUST-209, CUST-314. CS team sent status emails + workaround (retry logic) to older SDK users.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2427 (severity: P2). Paging sequence paused.
lia (sre): Final check: all services reporting <=0.5% 5xx, rolling 5m windows stable. Marking incident as mitigated, monitoring in watch window.
sanjay (oncall-azb): Thanks team :thumbsup: — solid coordination. Will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 1500 UTC.
